newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Malaysia rubber ends down, trade watches INRO.
newsitem.headline: Malaysia rubber ends down, trade watches INRO.

text.p: Malaysia's rubber market ended lower again on Monday, with dealers staying alert to any support that the International Natural Rubber Organisation (INRO) might show to prices in Tuesday's trading.

Under INRO's market intervention guidelines to support rubber prices, the group "may buy" rubber at 183 cents a kg and the daily indicator price on July 4, the last trading day before Monday, was at 184.89 Malaysian/Singapore cents a kg.
On July 3, the daily indicator was at 186.82.
The INRO's five-day moving average was at 190.03 on July 4 from 192.43 a day earlier.
"If the indicator falls again tomorrow, INRO might come in," said a trader on Monday.

At the close, the Malaysian Rubber Exchange and Licensing Board quoted August buyers of the benchmark RSS1 at 237 Malaysian/Singapore cents (95 U.S. cents) a kg, down six cents from Friday's close. August SMR20 was two cents off to 235.50.
A check with trading houses in the evening showed the SMR20 at offered 232, SMR10 at 234, SMR5 at 2457, SMR CV at 304, SMR L at 285 and drum latex at 202.
